title: Bankruptcy exemptions - federal and state interaction
facts: Bankruptcy exemptions determine what property a debtor may protect from liquidation or creditor claims within the bankruptcy process.
Federal bankruptcy law contains a federal exemption scheme, but states may opt out and require residents to use state exemptions; some states allow a choice subject to domicile rules.
Which exemption system applies can depend on where the debtor lived during statutory lookback periods, not simply the debtor's address on filing day.
A specific property-protection answer therefore requires the debtor's state and domicile history.
